primitives.name: First-second acceleration
primitives.verbatim_quote: Early acceleration is the change in smoothed speed over the first second after onset.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes constant sampling rate of 10 Hz, uses a centered three-frame median filter for smoothing, and defines movement onset as the first sample at or above 1 yd/s for two consecutive frames.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when Δt approaches zero or when smoothed velocity remains constant, leading to division by zero or zero acceleration.

layer2.mapping: Dual to NFL's 'explosiveness index' which models impulse divided by mass, but here directly observable from tracking data without biomechanical inverse dynamics.
layer2.telemetry: Residual variance after accounting for player weight and estimated force production capacity.

primitives.name: Attempt correlation coefficient
primitives.verbatim_quote: Attempt-level early-acceleration values correlated at Pearson r=0.792 and Spearman ρ=0.720.
primitives.assumptions: Correlation assumes linear relationship between paired measurements, homoscedasticity, and independence of observations; Spearman additionally assumes monotonicity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Correlation breaks down when data exhibit heteroscedasticity, non-monotonic relationships, or outliers that disproportionately influence the Pearson estimate.

layer2.mapping: Maps to NFL's intra-class correlation (ICC) for repeatability assessment, where high r/Spearman indicates low random measurement error relative to true score variance.
layer2.telemetry: Standard error of estimate (SEE) derived from r to quantify uncertainty in predicting one attempt from another.

primitives.name: Onset threshold detection
primitives.verbatim_quote: Movement onset is the first sample at or above 1 yd/s for two consecutive frames.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a fixed velocity threshold of 1 yd/s and requires two consecutive samples to confirm movement, reducing false positives from noise.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breakdown occurs when true onset happens below 1 yd/s, leading to delayed detection, or when noise causes spurious crossings of the threshold.

layer2.mapping: Derived from the NFL's 'reaction time' operationalization but adapted to track-only data without stimulus timestamps, focusing solely on kinematic initiation.
layer2.telemetry: Time difference between actual sprint start and detected onset, serving as a proxy for systematic bias in the measurement pipeline.

primitives.name: Smoothed speed calculation
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Operational definition Combine tracking is sampled at 10 Hz.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes uniform sampling interval and that the signal bandwidth is below Nyquist frequency (5 Hz) to avoid aliasing.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breakdown occurs due to undersampling rapid accelerations or decelerations, causing aliasing artifacts in the derived kinematics.

layer2.mapping: Equivalent to a moving average filter in discrete time, dual to a low-pass Butterworth filter in continuous systems, both designed to reduce high-frequency noise.
layer2.telemetry: Residual noise level after filtering, typically quantified as root-mean-square deviation from a reference kinematic model.
